source_review.notes: Reviewed eight references covering distributed ordering, integration patterns, data-intensive systems, the OASIS AMQP 1.0 standard, the CNCF CloudEvents 1.0.2 specification, transaction processing, asynchronous work beyond distributed transactions, and site reliability. Official OASIS, CNCF/GitHub, CIDR, Enterprise Integration Patterns, and Google SRE endpoints returned HTTP 200. The Lamport publisher DOI redirect returned access-control HTTP 403 while its stable bibliographic identity was checked separately. OASIS identifies AMQP 1.0 as an OASIS Standard dated 29 October 2012; the chapter identifies CloudEvents by the cited 1.0.2 tag and date rather than claiming it is the newest release.

evidence: Reviewed message identity, type, version, authority, partition key, source sequence, delivery-attempt set, effect, deduplication relation, arrival rate, sustainable capacity, backlog, drain-time, and scoped ordering notation.
Confirmed units are stated for messages per second, seconds, kilobytes, gigabytes, message counts, and raw payload estimates.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Delivery, processing, acknowledgment, consumer effect, and business outcome remain separate modeled states.

evidence: Recomputed the compact outage as 500 times 900 = 450000 messages and approximately 900 MB of raw payload at 2 KB each.
Recomputed Example 1 as 1200 times 1200 = 1440000 messages and 2.16 GB of raw payload at 1.5 KB each.
Recomputed Example 2 healthy capacity as 8 times 75 = 600/s, degraded capacity as 6 times 75 = 450/s, ten-minute growth as 30000 messages, and later drain time as 300 seconds at 100/s excess.
Recomputed Exercise 2 as 648000 messages, 1.62 GB raw payload, 1100/s restored capacity, 200/s excess, 3240 seconds or 54 minutes drain time, and 130/s growth with three consumers unavailable.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All byte estimates are explicitly raw decimal quantities and exclude envelope, index, replication, transaction, compression, and headroom effects.

evidence: Verified simplified backlog change as (arrival rate minus sustainable completion capacity) times interval.
Verified complete outage is the capacity-zero case and constant-rate drain time is backlog divided by positive excess capacity.
Verified source sequence classifications for duplicate, next, gap, and stale observations under one authoritative sequence.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter limits queue equations to simplified constant-rate models and distinguishes them from measured work cost, skew, downstream limits, retries, and unstable overload.

evidence: Reviewed crashes before and after producer commit, publication, relay checkpoint, consumer commit, acknowledgment, and external side effect.

Reviewed duplicate, missing, gap, stale, late, and out-of-order messages; mutable and hot partition keys; poison data; expiry; quarantine; broker partition; consumer slowdown; storage pressure; and replay.

Reviewed overbroad wildcard credentials, retained personal data, dead-letter exposure, credential rotation, pending payment, intermittent connectivity, late cancellation, and irreversible medication or shelter outcomes.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Cases span loss, duplication, delay, overload, compatibility, security, privacy, recovery, and safety-critical consequences.

evidence: Traced acceptance, authority, publication, duplicate tolerance, ordering, capacity, failure classification, compatibility, security, and evidence invariants throughout exposition and exercises.
Confirmed dead-letter placement, broker health, low backlog, handler success, and transport encryption are never treated as sufficient business correctness evidence.
invariant_checking.notes: Commands, events, documents, notifications, broker records, and derived state retain distinct semantics and ownership.

evidence: Reviewed the publication-gap argument and confirmed a crash can separate two independent writes regardless of their application-code order.
Reviewed the duplicate-delivery argument and confirmed commit-before-acknowledgment plus lost acknowledgment makes redelivery necessary under at-least-once recovery.
Confirmed the proposed mechanisms narrow but do not erase residual failures: outbox leaves duplicates, idempotency has identity and retention scope, and compensation can fail.
proof_review.notes: No unqualified exactly-once business effect, global ordering, atomic cross-system outcome, or reversible compensation theorem is claimed.

evidence: Audited uses of guarantee, exactly once, durable, atomic, authoritative, ordered, idempotent, safe, complete, proof, invariant, and evidence.
Verified delivery guarantees name scope and failure assumptions, while capacity calculations are labeled simplified estimates.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Models, mechanisms, policies, protocol capabilities, and business evidence are kept distinct.

empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The chapter prescribes crash, capacity, compatibility, security, replay, and recovery testing but presents no executed code, live broker, benchmark, or reproduced empirical study.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed asynchronous outcome boundaries, message intent, fact and command authority, lifecycle states, dual-write gaps, outbox, duplicate delivery, guarantee scope, ordering, partitioning, backlog, admission, retry, poison data, time semantics, choreography, orchestration, evolution, replay, security, observability, testing, and selection against synchronous or batch integration.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed relay checkpoints, inbox atomicity, external-effect ambiguity, per-key gaps, hot partitions, consumer loss, recovery headroom, poison-message handling, authorized redrive, expiry, schema rollback, replay isolation, wildcard credentials, archives, dead-letter stores, broker partitions, pending UX, and intermittent-connectivity reconciliation. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified first-principles messaging vocabulary, explicit lifecycle and queue models, sixteen misconceptions, ten distinct worked examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers ending in an unfamiliar emergency-shelter transfer problem.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. Source reachability and arithmetic checks do not constitute a live broker or failure-recovery experiment.
